signs.name: Codman triangle
signs.text: Periosteum lifted by the tumour forms a triangle of new bone at the edge of the lesion where it meets the cortex. Sign of an AGGRESSIVE process (osteosarcoma, Ewing; also infection).

signs.name: Sunburst periosteal reaction – osteosarcoma
signs.text: Spiculated periosteal new bone radiating perpendicular to the cortex around a dense metaphyseal tumour of the knee – osteogenic osteosarcoma (10–25 y).

signs.name: Onion-skin (lamellated) periosteal reaction – Ewing sarcoma
signs.text: Several parallel layers of periosteal new bone around a permeative diaphyseal lesion in a child or adolescent – Ewing sarcoma.

signs.name: Nidus – osteoid osteoma (CT)
signs.text: Small (< 1.5–2 cm) round lucent nidus, ± central calcification, inside dense reactive cortical sclerosis. CT shows it best. Night pain relieved by aspirin.

signs.name: Fluid–fluid levels – aneurysmal bone cyst (MRI)
signs.text: Horizontal interfaces between layered blood products in multiple cystic cavities on T2/STIR – aneurysmal bone cyst (expansile, eccentric, metaphyseal, child).

signs.name: Ivory vertebrae – osteoblastic metastases
signs.text: Diffuse homogeneous increase in density of a vertebral body with normal size and preserved discs. Adults: blastic metastases (prostate, breast), lymphoma, Paget.

signs.name: Bamboo spine – syndesmophytes
signs.text: Thin vertical marginal ossifications bridging all vertebral bodies give the bamboo appearance – late ankylosing spondylitis.

signs.name: Dagger and trolley-track signs – ankylosing spondylitis
signs.text: AP view: a central dense line (ossified supraspinous/interspinous ligaments) = dagger sign; two lateral lines (ossified facet capsules) = trolley track.

signs.name: Heberden & Bouchard nodes – hand osteoarthritis
signs.text: Joint-space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis and marginal osteophytes of the DIP (Heberden) and PIP (Bouchard) joints; bone density normal.

signs.name: Rheumatoid arthritis – symmetric MCP / wrist disease
signs.text: Bilateral SYMMETRIC involvement of MCP, PIP and wrist joints: juxta-articular osteopenia, marginal erosions, uniform narrowing (DIP spared).

signs.name: Coxarthrosis
signs.text: Asymmetric (superolateral) joint-space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, geodes and marginal osteophytes of the hip.

signs.name: Punched-out lesions – multiple myeloma
signs.text: Multiple small round sharply delineated lytic lesions without sclerotic rim in the skull/spine/pelvis of an older adult; bone scan often negative.

signs.name: Osteochondroma (exostosis)
signs.text: Bony outgrowth from the metaphysis pointing AWAY from the joint, its cortex and medulla continuous with the host bone.

signs.name: Chondroid calcifications – chondrosarcoma
signs.text: Adult, pelvis/proximal femur: lytic destructive lesion with chondroid (rings and arcs) calcifications and soft-tissue mass.

signs.name: Chronic osteomyelitis – sclerosis & cortical thickening
signs.text: Chronic infection: thick irregular sclerotic cortex (involucrum), ± sequestrum (dense fragment in a lucent bed) and cloaca.

signs.name: Horseshoe kidney (IVU)
shapes: lower poles fused in front of the spine
signs.text: Low kidneys with medially oriented lower calyces and long axes converging inferiorly – the isthmus joins the lower poles in front of the aorta.

signs.name: Bilateral ureterocele – "cobra head"
signs.text: Bulbous dilatation of the intramural ureters protruding into the contrast-filled bladder with a thin lucent halo (the ureteral wall).

signs.name: UPJ obstruction (IVU)
signs.text: Hydronephrosis with a dilated pelvis and delayed excretion, but a normal/collapsed ureter below → obstruction at the ureteropelvic junction.

signs.name: Polycystic kidney disease (CT)
signs.text: Bilaterally enlarged kidneys replaced by innumerable water-density cysts of various sizes; check the liver for cysts.

signs.name: Angiomyolipoma – hyperechoic renal mass (US)
signs.text: Well-defined hyperechoic renal lesion; CT confirms macroscopic fat (negative HU) – the only renal tumour diagnosed by imaging alone.

signs.name: Nephrocalcinosis (KUB)
signs.text: Fine, clustered, bilateral calcifications projecting over the renal medulla (pyramids).

signs.name: Bilateral adrenal myelolipoma (CT)
signs.text: Adrenal masses containing macroscopic FAT (as dark as subcutaneous fat, negative HU) – specific and benign.

signs.name: Retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy (CT)
signs.text: Rounded soft-tissue masses around the aorta and IVC with short axis > 10 mm – lymphoma, testicular or pelvic cancer.

signs.name: Achalasia – bird's beak
signs.text: Dilated, aperistaltic oesophagus ending in a SHORT smooth symmetric tapering at the gastro-oesophageal junction; air–fluid level; no gastric air bubble.

signs.name: Benign oesophageal stricture
signs.text: Long, regular, symmetric (axial) and progressive narrowing of the distal oesophagus with upstream dilatation – peptic or caustic.

signs.name: Oesophageal cancer – irregular stenosis
signs.text: Short, eccentric, irregular stenosis with abrupt edges (shouldering) and mucosal destruction – malignancy until proven otherwise.

signs.name: Oesophageal diverticulum – addition image
signs.text: Barium projecting OUTSIDE the normal contour through a neck = addition image (mid-oesophageal traction diverticulum).

signs.name: Target (bull's eye) lesion – liver metastasis (US)
signs.text: A hypoechoic rim around an iso/hyperechoic centre is the classic US appearance of a metastasis.

signs.name: Spoke-wheel vessels – FNH (Doppler)
signs.text: A central feeding artery with radiating branches ("spoke-wheel") inside a liver lesion of a young woman = focal nodular hyperplasia.

signs.name: Hydatid cyst – detached membrane
signs.text: Echinococcal cyst with a detached, floating laminated membrane (Gharbi type II) – also daughter cysts or calcified wall in later stages.

signs.name: Chronic pancreatitis – calcifications & duct
signs.text: Parenchymal calcifications and a dilated, irregular (moniliform) Wirsung duct – chronic pancreatitis (steatorrhoea = exocrine failure).

signs.name: Haemangioma – centripetal fill-in (4 phases)
signs.text: Peripheral, discontinuous nodular enhancement in the arterial phase that progressively fills the lesion centripetally – hepatic haemangioma.

multi.title: Kidney stone
multi.note: All calcium stones are white on X-ray and CT; US shows the shadow and the hydronephrosis. Uric-acid stones: invisible on KUB, visible on CT.

multi.title: Hydronephrosis
multi.note: US is first-line: no contrast, no radiation; IVU shows function and level; chronic obstruction thins the cortex.

multi.title: Horseshoe kidney
multi.note: Projection techniques show the axes; CT shows the isthmus and complications.

multi.title: Polycystic kidney disease
multi.note: IVU only suggests it from distorted calyces; CT/US see the cysts directly.

multi.title: Bladder stone vs tumour
multi.note: Stone = mobile + shadow; tumour = fixed + flow; clot = mobile, no flow, no shadow.

multi.title: Osteoid osteoma
multi.note: X-ray shows the reaction; CT finds the nidus (the actual tumour).

multi.title: Aneurysmal bone cyst
multi.note: X-ray shows the shape; MRI proves the blood-filled cavities.

multi.title: Bone metastases
multi.note: X-ray needs 30–50 % mineral loss; CT shows cortex; MRI shows marrow earliest; bone scan the whole skeleton.

multi.title: Ankylosing spondylitis
multi.note: Sacroiliitis comes first; CT/MRI see it earlier than X-ray.

multi.title: Chondrosarcoma
multi.note: Rings-and-arcs calcifications = cartilage tumour; aggressive features = malignant.

multi.title: Hydatid cyst
multi.note: US classifies the stage (Gharbi/WHO); CT for extent and complications.

multi.title: Liver haemangioma
multi.note: US suggests it, multiphase CT/MRI prove it.

multi.title: FNH
multi.note: FNH contains hepatocytes → takes up gadoxetic acid (adenoma and metastases do not).

multi.title: Chronic pancreatitis
multi.note: CT is best for calcifications; MRCP for the duct.

epiphysis.key: Eccentric lytic, reaches subchondral bone, no rim

pairs.ex: Osteophytes are horizontal-then-curved and triangular (degeneration); syndesmophytes are thin and vertical, bridging the corners.
Malignant: short, eccentric, irregular, shouldered. Benign: long, smooth, axial, tapered.
Achalasia: massively dilated oesophagus with a smooth short bird's beak; cancer: irregular stricture with mild dilatation.
RA: symmetric MCP/wrist, osteopenia, erosions, deformities. OA: DIP/PIP osteophytes, normal density.
Gout: asymmetric punched-out erosions with overhanging edges and tophi, normal density (1st MTP).

pairs.q: Which bone tumour is in the DIAPHYSIS (Ewing)?
pairs.ex: Osteosarcoma: metaphysis around the knee, sunburst. Ewing: diaphysis, onion skin, big soft-tissue mass.
Congenital: waist at the rudimentary disc, normal total height. Acquired (post-infection): no waist, lost height, kyphosis.

pairs.q: Which renal lesion is a SIMPLE CYST?
pairs.ex: Cyst: round, homogeneous water density, thin wall, no enhancement. RCC: solid, heterogeneous, enhancing.

pairs.q: Which bladder lesion is a STONE?
pairs.ex: Stone: echogenic, posterior acoustic shadow, moves with position. Tumour: fixed wall mass with flow.

pairs.q: Which is a primary malignant bone tumour (not infection)?
pairs.ex: Both can show periosteal reaction; tumour = mass with matrix and Codman; infection = sclerosis, sequestrum, sinus tract.
ADPKD: large kidneys full of cysts. Horseshoe: normal parenchyma, lower poles joined by an isthmus.

pairs.q: Which liver lesion is a METASTASIS?
pairs.ex: Metastasis: hypoechoic halo (target), often multiple. Haemangioma: homogeneous, well-defined, hyperechoic.
